title: Through All This Life's Eventful Road
description: Through All This Life's Eventful Road in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 66, “Walking with God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through all this life's e-vent-ful road, Fain would I walk with Thee, my God, And make Thy pre-sence light a-round, And ev-ery step on ho-ly ground.

lines: Through all this life's eventful road,
Fain would I walk with Thee, my God,
And make Thy presence light around,
And every step on holy ground.
Each blessing would I trace to Thee,
In every grief Thy mercy see;
And through the paths of duty move,
And when the angel Death stands by,
Be this my strength, that Thou art nigh;
And this my joy, that I shall be
With those who dwell in light with Thee.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
